scenes.title: Key ideas
scenes.vo: First, Vote-escrow: you lock a governance token for a period (often up to 4 years) and get ve-tokens with voting power that decays as the unlock approaches. Longer lock equals more power. Next, Gauges: ve-holders vote on which pools receive the protocol's token emissions. Emissions attract liquidity, so votes are valuable. Then, Bribes or voting incentives: protocols that want liquidity pay ve-holders to vote for their pool. Voters earn this as yield (plus a share of fees in some designs). Also, Liquid lockers or meta-governance: protocols that lock on your behalf and give you a tradable token. It's liquid, but it can trade at a discount, and it adds a layer of risk. And finally, Risks: long locks (you can't sell), the token's price over the lock, emissions diluting holders, and governance capture.

scenes.vo: Let's work an example, step by step. $10,000 of a ve-token earning about 15% A.P.R. in bribes about $1,500 a year, paid in various tokens. But the underlying is locked for 4 years: if the token falls 60%, the position is worth $4,000 plus the bribes collected. A liquid-locker version lets you exit, but it traded at a 20% discount during the last sell-off. Price the lock, not just the A.P.R.
